faqs.question: What should a Halloween party invitation say?
faqs.answer: It needs five details: the date with a start and end time, the address with parking notes, the costume rule (required, optional or none), the food arrangement, and an RSVP-by date with one way to reply. Put the date and costume rule first, because many guests read the invite in a phone preview.

faqs.question: How do I word a Halloween invitation for an adults-only party?
faqs.answer: Write "adults only" in plain words rather than relying on a dark headline, and add a finish time so guests can book a babysitter. A line like "Costume encouraged, adults only, reply by [date]" covers it without sounding stern.

faqs.question: How do I say no plus-ones on a Halloween invite without being rude?
faqs.answer: Give a reason that is about space, not about the guest, such as "Our flat fits 14 ghosts at most, so this invitation is just for you." The Emily Post Institute's guidance is that an invitation covers only the people named, so you are stating a norm, not inventing a rule.

faqs.question: How do I ask guests about food allergies on an invitation?
faqs.answer: Fold it into the RSVP and offer a private route, for example "Dietary needs? Message me privately." Research on food-allergy social anxiety describes people worrying about seeming demanding when they decline food, so making the question routine helps them answer.

faqs.question: What should I write when costumes are optional?
faqs.answer: Say "costume optional" and offer an easy middle step, such as one orange item or a single spooky accessory. Without that, half the guests worry they will be underdressed and the other half overthink it.

faqs.question: How should I word an office Halloween party invitation?
faqs.answer: Keep costumes clearly optional and work-appropriate, rule out masks that cover faces, and hold the event inside working hours where you can. Not every colleague celebrates Halloween, so the wording should make sitting it out feel normal.

faqs.question: What goes in a murder mystery Halloween invitation?
faqs.answer: The date, time, address and an earlier RSVP deadline than usual, because every guest needs a character. Send each role and costume brief privately after someone says yes, never in the group message, so the culprit stays secret.

faqs.question: Is it rude to send a Halloween party invite only a few days before?
faqs.answer: No, as long as the wording admits the short notice and keeps expectations low, for example "Short notice, long night, costume or work clothes." Give a same-day or next-day reply time so you still get a headcount.

faqs.question: How do I follow up with guests who haven't replied?
faqs.answer: Contact them directly, sound friendly rather than hurt, and give a concrete reason such as a food order on a named day. Mentioning which friends are already coming can also help, since attendance at group events tends to track whether friends attend.

faqs.question: Can I send my Halloween party invitations with SubhSandesh?
faqs.answer: No. SubhSandesh's Halloween page is a one-person greeting with partner, bestie, family and kids modes; it does not send to a group or track RSVPs. Use it for the one friend who can't come, and use your usual messaging app for the guest list.

faqs.question: What date is Halloween?
faqs.answer: Halloween is on 31 October every year. It falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027, so a party on the night itself is easy to plan in either year.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Party Invitation Wording: 30 Invites by Party Type

Good Halloween party invitation wording names the kind of party, gives five details (date and time, address, costume rule, food, RSVP-by date) and sets the tone in under 50 words. Lead with the date and costume rule: 48.3% of pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on a phone, where a preview shows only the opening line.

Our nearest seasonal data is Raksha Bandhan 2026, a different occasion and a small sample (n = 89), yet 49.4% of those pages were built on the festival day itself, so a stated deadline does your chasing. Below: 30 invitations across ten party types, plus allergy and plus-one lines.

## The 5 details every Halloween party invitation needs

Every invitation here runs headline, details, dress code, RSVP. The [Emily Post Institute's invitation etiquette guide](https://emilypost.com/advice/invitation-etiquette) (undated) asks guests to reply within a day or two and by the deadline at the latest, which only works if you set one.

- **Date and time:** a start and a finish, such as "31 October, 7 to 11 pm".
- **Address and parking:** the full address plus where to park or which buzzer to press.
- **Costume rule:** required, optional or none, in those exact words.
- **Food and drink:** served, potluck or bring-your-own.
- **RSVP-by date:** one date and one way to answer.

### Asking about allergies without singling anyone out

A 2025 paper in *Pediatric Allergy and Immunology* describes [food-allergy social anxiety](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12400901), the fear of seeming demanding or ungrateful when declining unsafe food. I read only the abstract, which concerns young people; the fix still applies: ask privately, inside the RSVP.

- "When you reply, mention any allergies or foods you skip. I'd rather plan than guess."
- "Allergy, vegetarian or halal? One line with your answer is plenty."
- "Dietary needs? Message me privately and your safe plates will carry a label."

### Saying "no plus-ones" politely

The same Emily Post guide is blunt: an invitation covers only the people named, and if a date or children are welcome, it says so. Make that clear without sounding cold.

- "Our flat fits 14 ghosts at most, so this invitation is just for you."
- "We're keeping it to the names on this message. Thank you for understanding."
- "Partners welcome: add their name when you reply."

## 30 Halloween party invitations, grouped by party type

Swap your details into the brackets. Puns stay light: the party type sets the tone.

### Adults-only Halloween party invitations

Write "adults only" in plain words, not just a dark headline. A finish time helps anyone booking a babysitter.

- **After Dark: Grown-Ups Only**  
  31 October, 8 pm to midnight, [address]  
  Costume encouraged · Reply by [date]
- **The Kids Are Asleep. The Candles Are Lit.**  
  Cocktails at [name]'s, [date], 9 pm · Dress dark or dress up  
  Tell me by [date]
- **A Late Supper for the Recently Deceased**  
  Three courses by candlelight, [date], 7:30 pm  
  Come as anyone who died dramatically · Answer by [date]

### Kids' Halloween party invitations

The child gets the headline, the parent gets the pick-up time. Say whether parents should stay.

- **[Name] Is Turning 7 and Turning Into a Bat**  
  [date], 3 to 5 pm, [address] · Friendly costumes welcome  
  Parents of under-5s please stay · RSVP by [date]
- **Pumpkins, Paint and Party Bags**  
  [date], 2 to 4 pm · Wear clothes that can meet paint  
  Reply by [date]
- **A Not-Too-Spooky Party for Ages 4 to 8**  
  [date], 10:30 am, [venue] · Costumes optional, masks off for games  
  Text [number] by [date] with any allergies

### Family Halloween party invitations

A family invite must suit a toddler and a grandparent. Start early and keep adult costumes optional.

- **All Ages, All Monsters**  
  [date], 4 to 8 pm · Costumes for anyone who wants one  
  Reply by [date] with adult and child numbers
- **Trick-or-Treat Together, Then Supper at Ours**  
  31 October: meet 5:30 pm, walk at 6, eat at 7:30 · Bring a torch  
  RSVP by [date]
- **The [Surname] Haunted Garden Is Open**  
  Lantern trail, [date], 5 to 7 pm · Quiet room upstairs  
  Let us know by [date]

### Office Halloween party invitations

At work, costumes must be genuinely optional and the event should sit inside working hours. Not every colleague celebrates Halloween.

- **Halloween Lunch on the Fourth Floor**  
  [date], 12:30 to 2 pm · Costumes optional, no face-covering masks  
  Sign up by [date]
- **The Great Desk Pumpkin Contest**  
  Judging [date], 4 pm, 3 prizes · A sticky-note pumpkin counts  
  Enter by [date]
- **Team Halloween Quiz, 45 Minutes**  
  [date], 3 pm, boardroom or [video link] · Cat ears suffice  
  Reply in the thread by [date]

### Costume-required party invitations

Write "required" and say what counts. A low minimum, like a hat and a backstory, stops guests skipping over the cost of an outfit.

- **No Costume, No Entry (We Mean It)**  
  [date], 8 pm, [address] · A hat plus a backstory qualifies  
  RSVP by [date] with who you're coming as
- **Come as Your Worst Fear**  
  [date], 9 pm · Costume required, interpreted freely  
  Reply by [date]
- **Monsters of the Silver Screen**  
  [date], 7:30 pm · Required: a character from any film made before 1970  
  Answer by [date]

### Costume-optional party invitations

"Optional" must read as truly optional, or half the room feels underdressed. Offer a middle step, like one orange item.

- **Dress Up, Dress Down, Just Turn Up**  
  Drinks, [date], 8 pm · One spooky accessory is perfect  
  Reply by [date]
- **Orange Is the Dress Code**  
  [date], 7 pm · Wear anything orange, or don't  
  Yes or no by [date], please
- **Come as You Are, or Come as a Vampire**  
  [date], 8 pm, [address] · Costume entirely up to you  
  Let me know by [date]

### Murder mystery party invitations

Every guest needs a character, so you need answers earlier. Send each role privately after a yes.

- **Someone Won't Survive Dinner on [date]**  
  7 pm, [address] · Your character brief follows your reply  
  RSVP by [date] so we can cast the suspects
- **Death at [Surname] Manor, 1926**  
  [date], 7:30 pm · Dress for the era, arrive in character  
  Confirm by [date]
- **The Séance Went Wrong**  
  [date], 8 pm · Eight guests, one culprit  
  Reply by [date] with anything you won't eat

### Potluck Halloween party invitations

Name what you need, or you'll get six bags of crisps. Ask for allergen labels on every dish.

- **Bring a Dish, Bring a Ghost Story**  
  [date], 6:30 pm · Please label what's in your dish  
  Pick mains, sides or puddings by [date]
- **The Pumpkin Potluck**  
  Every dish contains pumpkin, [date], 7 pm  
  Tell me your dish by [date] so we avoid five soups
- **Cauldron Night: You Bring the Contents**  
  Soup potluck, [date], 7 pm · We supply bowls and bread  
  Reply by [date] with what you're making

### Halloween dinner invitations (Friendsgiving-style)

A seated dinner needs exact numbers, so the reply date matters more. Ask about diets in the same line.

- **A Long Table on All Hallows' Eve**  
  Dinner for twelve, 31 October, 7 pm · Dark colours, no costume needed  
  Reply by [date] with any dietary needs
- **Friends, Food and a Few Ghosts**  
  [date], 6:30 pm · Bring a dessert or a bottle, nothing more  
  Final call [date]
- **Supper by Jack-o'-Lantern Light**  
  Set menu, [date], 7:30 pm · Smart-casual  
  Diet notes by [date], please

### Last-minute and same-week Halloween invitations

Admit the short notice and keep the bar low. In the same Raksha Bandhan sample, 86.1% of on-time pages were built within 24 hours of the festival, so late plans are normal.

- **Short Notice, Long Night**  
  [day], 8 pm at mine · Costume or work clothes  
  A quick yes or no by [day]
- **Plans Fell Through? Ours Didn't.**  
  Pizza and horror films, tonight, 7:30 pm · Pyjamas count as a costume  
  Reply by 5 pm
- **Spare Pumpkins, Spare Seats**  
  Carving night, [day], 6 pm · Tools provided  
  Text me by noon tomorrow

## Which wording fits which Halloween party?

Five tone bands cover all ten party types. Find your row, then borrow the headline.

| Party type | Tone | Must include | Example headline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Adults-only, costume-required | Dark, dry | "Adults only" in words; a costume minimum | After Dark: Grown-Ups Only |
| Kids', family | Warm, not scary | Ages, pick-up time, whether parents stay | Pumpkins, Paint and Party Bags |
| Office | Light, inclusive | Optional costumes, no face-covering masks | Halloween Lunch on the Fourth Floor |
| Murder mystery, dinner | Theatrical, precise | Earlier RSVP, role or menu note, diet line | Someone Won't Survive Dinner |
| Potluck, last-minute | Casual, honest | What to bring; a same-day reply time | Short Notice, Long Night |

The more a party depends on exact numbers, the earlier and firmer the reply date. That is why dinners and murder mysteries ask first.

## How to chase a missing RSVP without sounding hurt

The Emily Post Institute's note on [what to do when guests don't RSVP](https://emilypost.com/advice/what-to-do-when-guests-dont-rsvp) (undated) calls it perfectly polite to contact non-repliers, if you sound friendly rather than accusatory. Give a reason, such as a food order.

Naming who is coming may help. A 2017 *PLOS ONE* study of Meetup groups by [Smiljanić and Mitrović Dankulov](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC5293197) found small events mostly strengthen existing ties, and cites earlier work where a member's chance of attending depended strongly on whether friends would attend.

- "Hi [name], checking the Halloween invite reached you. I'm ordering food on [day]; are you in?"
- "No pressure either way, but [friend] and [friend] are coming and asked about you."

## Where SubhSandesh fits: one guest, not the guest list

SubhSandesh is not an invitation tool: nothing here sends to a group or tracks RSVPs. Our [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is a one-person greeting page, English only, with partner, bestie, family and kids modes. Send it to the friend who can't come: they carve a pumpkin until your word glows and save a 1080×1920 Boo License.

Inviting one date? [The Invitation](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) asks a question they have to answer, and yes starts a countdown to the plan. For 20 guests, your usual messaging app wins: our pages average 11.1 views each, which fits one person returning, not a crowd.

## Sources

- Emily Post Institute, "Invitation Etiquette", undated, checked 13 October 2026.
- Emily Post Institute, "What to Do When Guests Don't RSVP", undated, checked 13 October 2026.
- Engel et al., food-allergy social anxiety, *Pediatric Allergy and Immunology*, 1 September 2025 (abstract read).
- Smiljanić and Mitrović Dankulov, event participation dynamics, *PLOS ONE*, 6 February 2017.
